no_new_call_note: The live register remains empty, so there was nothing to review or post-mortem this week. On the hunt itself: the East-West pipeline shutdown and the Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab disruption are already the lead story across Bloomberg, Reuters and the general wires, with the Baltic Dry Index's record level and distillate stocks below every comparable week in the 2021-2025 envelope both reported throughout the week of September 14-18 - not ahead of where attention already sits. The Senate's failure to advance the CLARITY Act past its procedural vote was reported by CNBC and the financial press from September 1 onward, so its resolution this month is already folded into general commentary rather than a fresh variant against consensus. The forecast copper deficit tied to Zambian smelter maintenance and the Indonesian smelter outage has been argued in mining trade press since the second quarter and remains a running narrative, not a new dated development. Brazil's wheat and corn production cuts trace back to USDA reports published across April, June and August, with nothing new this week to change the thesis. The nuclear and uranium build-out - reactor funding, enrichment contracts, utility buying - has been the subject of Department of Energy announcements and mainstream sector write-ups since January, and the uranium-term-price-versus-junior-miner gap is the same argument specialist mining press has run since the second quarter. A Nuvectis Pharma FDA decision landed September 18, but an approval is priced the moment it publishes and carries no forward variant to hold a kill condition against. Nothing found this week was simultaneously new, confirmed by more than one independent source, and still ahead of where the market's attention already sits - so no call was opened. An empty week is counted, not apologized for.
